newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles economic rebound continues - BankAmerica.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles economic rebound continues - BankAmerica.

text.p: Los Angeles County's economy has rebounded, reflecting recent gains in employment, tourism and trade, according to a Bank of America report released on Monday.
"The preponderance of evidence suggests that Los Angeles is coming back," said Howard Roth, director of regional economics at BankAmerica Corp unit Bank of America.
Although employment remains below pre-recession levels, Los Angeles County has added 180,000 jobs since 1994, according to Roth's report.
The job growth has been broad-based, with a relatively high percentage of the new jobs in high-paying industries like movie production and computer and data processing services.
"If present trends continue, it won't be long before Los Angeles has more high-paying jobs than ever," Roth said.
Tourism, the county's third largest industry, has also regained momentum. Last year, visitors spent $10.5 billion in Los Angeles, 26 percent more than in 1990, the report said.
The county's film industry, one of the draws for tourists, continued to grow despite the recession, increasing employment by 26 percent between 1990 and 1994.
By 1996, the county's film industry employed 224,000 people. This expansion should continue, Roth said.
Trade has also remained a stable source of economic strength for the county, the Bank of America report said.

Annual growth of trade in the Los Angeles customs district has averaged 9.0 percent since 1987. In 1996, $170 billion in goods passed through the district, primarily through the ports of Long Beach and Los Angeles, the report said.
